_comment: Source of truth for the accountant sign-off register. docs/insurance-brokerage/ACCOUNTANT_PACK.md section 16 is GENERATED from this file by scripts/gen-signoff-register.mjs. Validated in CI by scripts/check-signoff-register.mjs, which checks the setting exists with the allowed values AND that declared evidence files exist. It cannot prove accounting behaviour is correct: that is what the evidence and the reviewed_at field are for.

items.decision: Gross premium is recognised at bind as a receivable from the client and a payable to the insurer. A receipt taken before bind is a liability (unallocated client advance) until and unless a policy binds, at which point it is allocated against that policy's receivable rather than recognised as new cash.
items.note: Unallocated advances are built (B2), including the release-on-bind path, so a pre-bind receipt has somewhere to sit and a policy to be applied to. What keeps this partial is evidence, not code: the migration and test have been parse-checked but never executed against a database.

items.area: Insurer settlement: gross basis and net exceptions
items.decision: The insurer payable is booked gross and commission is a separate receivable (1110), never a deduction from what the insurer is owed. A net-settlement arrangement is a controlled exception requiring a documented insurer agreement, legal confirmation, accountant approval, an effective date and audit history, scoped to that insurer agreement.
items.note: Open legal question: whether any insurer agreement may lawfully set off commission against premium without conflicting with Insurance Act s.90(3).

items.decision: Recognition follows the insurer agreement, in four selectable modes: at_placement (unconditional entitlement at bind), on_premium_collection (earned when the client's receipt covers the premium; a partial receipt earns nothing), pro_rata_on_collection (earned proportionally to premium collected), on_insurer_settlement (earned when the insurer's item is settled). Every policy must have an explicit mode in force at bind; there is no silent default.
items.note: Four modes are selectable and implemented after 20261124010000/011000; the register keeps implemented:false for A3 until test_ins_commission_pro_rata.sql has passed on a clean replay. on_premium_collection remains BINARY by design (a partial receipt earns nothing); pro_rata_on_collection is the proportional mode. over_policy_term is not implemented and cannot be selected; the fourth implemented mode is pro_rata_on_collection, which the allowed_values list above omits. Fail-closed (decision 2) is in the same migration: bind refuses when no approved mode is in force. Decision 2B (per insurer) is built as B3: ins_insurer_commission_terms holds the mode agreed with each insurer, and it outranks the company setting at bind.

items.decision: Where the agreement is pro-rata, commission is earned in proportion to premium collected and the unearned balance remains in 2020. On cancellation, clawback is proportional to the approved return premium and may never exceed commission previously recognised; it is absorbed by the deferred pool first, then reverses recognised income, then becomes a recoverable from operating funds, replenishing client money where necessary.
items.note: pro_rata_on_collection is implemented by 20261124010100 (setting) and 20261124010200 (reader) BUT implemented stays false: the proof is supabase/tests/test_ins_commission_pro_rata.sql, which has been written and parse-checked, not executed. Flip it only when that test has passed on a clean replay. The cancellation clawback ordering (deferred, then income, then recoverable) is built and tested.

items.decision: Each participating insurer carries its own participation percentage, lead status, commission rate, settlement method, recognition trigger and tax treatment. Shares must total 100% with exactly one lead insurer. The allocation of premium, commission, liabilities, receipts, remittances and cancellation adjustments follows those shares.
items.note: 100% / single-lead enforcement is applied at bind and at approval.

items.decision: A cancellation preserves the original policy and financial history and distinguishes request date, effective date and financial settlement date. Return premium requested, approved, received and refunded are separate states; an approved refund is never treated as cash received, and no insurer receivable is raised merely because a refund was requested. The difference between original and return premium is never automatically brokerage income: insurer-retained short-period premium belongs to the insurer, brokerage fees only where contractually authorised, and statutory charges to their statutory recipient.
items.note: Three separate cancellation date fields are built as B4: request date (proposed_at), effective date and settlement date, with evidence required before an effective date can be backdated.

items.decision: Insurer-direct claims record administration, the insurer's decision and payment evidence, and never create brokerage cash, bank or payable entries. Brokerage-managed claims record the insurer receivable, funds received, the claimant payable and payments. Internal approval alone never creates a payment posting. Recoveries (overpayments, third-party, insurer underpayment, instalment) and authorised write-offs are recognised separately and never as a reduction of commission.
items.note: Two operating models, excess handling, reserve revisions, the stage model (B5) and recoveries and write-offs (B8) are built. Appendix B decisions of 2026-11-22 applied: Q1 a dedicated contra-claims-expense account (role ins_claim_write_off_expense) rather than a bad-debt account, with the insurer receivable pursued separately; Q4 recoveries credit the same account and are not netted into insurer receivables by default; Q3 repudiation is the ninth state, with the insurer's decision and reference recorded and reopening allowed. Write-off and recovery remain separately identifiable by journal source type, disposition kind and narrative, per the accountant's condition.

items.decision: Books remain in UGX. The policy exchange rate at bind is preserved and is not replaced by later market rates except through an authorised amendment or reversal. Original currency value, the UGX equivalent at bind, the settlement rate and realised and unrealised gain or loss are tracked separately, with rate overrides before bind requiring authority, reason and audit history.
items.note: Rates are held to 8 decimals. Revaluation runs through fin_revalue_fx at period end.

items.decision: The cut-over date is the day before production go-live. Existing policies are imported as existing business with original inception and expiry dates preserved, not treated as newly issued. Opening balances distinguish historical bills, receipts, receivables, payables, earned and deferred commission, claims balances, statutory liabilities and currency balances. Historical receipts and bills already represented in opening balances are not re-posted. Every migrated record carries a migration identifier and traceable source. Material unexplained differences prevent migration approval.
items.note: Opening balances are gated: one post per company, and a correction requires an explicit reopen with a reason.

items.decision: A closed period may be reopened only with a documented reason, senior finance approval, independent maker-checker approval, audit history, reclosure and retention of revised period-end reports; the requester never approves their own reopening. Manual journals must balance, carry finance maker and independent checker, state evidence and reason, reference the subledger for control-account entries, and be immutable once posted, corrected only by reversal or authorised adjustment. Manual journals must not silently create a difference between the general ledger and an operational subledger.
items.note: Period controls and the reversal rule exist, and a manual-journal path with maker-checker, evidence, figures frozen at submission and a subledger-reference requirement for control accounts is built (B6). Amount-based approval limits now exist for manual journals and a journal routed above level 1 is approved through every level rather than refused (B12). Still partial: the pack also asks for an extra tier for restricted accounts, and no GL account is marked restricted, so that tier does not exist. Currency and branch are not part of the routing key either.

items.decision: Approval limits are configurable by transaction type, amount, currency, role, level and branch, applied separately to refunds, insurer remittances, commission transfers, claim payments, intermediary commissions and manual journals, with multi-level approval, escalation, effective dates and audit history. Splitting a transaction to stay under a threshold is prevented.
items.note: Refunds of client advances route through an approval-limit engine with per-user limits, self-approval refusal and split detection (B7), and the refund function itself refuses without an approved request. Manual journals route by amount and, above level 1, are approved level by level before anything posts (B12). Still partial, for three stated reasons: the routing key is amount and role only, so currency, branch and department are not part of it; the requirement asks for escalation, which is not built for any transaction type; and insurer remittances, commission transfers and claim payments still do not route through the engine at all. Multi-level approval exists for manual journals only -- refunds remain single-approval at a routed level.

items.decision: Client money is strictly separated from operating money: separate bank accounts with distinct GL accounts, corresponding client-money liability and control accounts, tracking of amounts owed to insurers, clients and beneficiaries, prevention of transfers leaving the client-money position short, commission transfers only where entitlement is established, and appropriate approvals and audit history. A designated officer completes a daily client-money reconciliation and a separate person independently reviews it, comparing bank balance, cashbook, client-money liabilities, unallocated advances, available commission and unmatched items; missed reconciliations are escalated. A suspected shortage raises a high-priority alert and incident record, notifies management, restricts commission transfers and non-essential withdrawals, and requires independent approval to release those restrictions, distinguishing a genuine shortage from delayed bank feeds.
items.note: Segregation is enforced hard, and the three items the pack names are built (B9): a transfer is refused when it would leave the client-money POSITION negative (held less what is owed to clients and insurers, which is stronger than the balance test beside it); a negative position raises a shortage that blocks transfers until an independent release; and two consecutive missed reviewed reconciliations escalate. Still partial on one operational point: nothing runs the daily check on a schedule yet, so escalation only happens when something invokes it.

items.decision: Statutory charges are versioned catalogue entries naming legal basis, insurance class, calculation basis, rate, exemptions, collector, remitter, statutory recipient, payable account and effective date. No unverified rate may be active as a mandatory production charge. The Insurance Training Levy (0.5% of gross direct premium) is verified; the IRA levy and stamp duty are not and must remain inactive until an instrument is cited.
items.note: A rate cannot be marked verified without a source reference. enforcement=required raises the premium of every policy bound thereafter, which is why advisory is the default and why the choice is the accountant's.

items.area: VAT, withholding tax and broker-fee classification
items.decision: Every broker fee declares its class: insurance_brokerage (exempt under Schedule 3 of the VAT Act) or other_taxable_service, the latter requiring a stated reason. The exemption is the default and departing from it is a recorded decision. Agent and intermediary commission tax treatment is configurable per agreement and never assumed uniform. Withheld tax is an asset (1210), never a reduction of revenue and never a liability of the brokerage. The former ins.broker_fee_vat setting is withdrawn; classification, not a company-wide switch, governs the treatment.
items.note: ins.broker_fee_vat is deleted by 20261124010000. Client-side WHT on a client-paid brokerage fee is not automatically applied and the rate is seeded unapproved: accountant confirmation is required before activation.

items.decision: Intermediary registration, agency agreements and commission accrual/payment are separate concerns. The register distinguishes insurer-appointed agents, independent brokers, sub-agents and referral partners, each agreement carrying its own rates, tax settings and accrual trigger. Accrual and payment remain subject to accountant approval of the accounting treatment and legal confirmation of Ugandan sub-agency requirements. Agents are never treated as employees.
items.note: Agent share is an expense (5010), not a netting of the brokerage's own commission. The expense-versus-netting question needs the accountant's confirmation.

items.decision: Reporting supports PDF and Excel exports and printable layouts, filtered by date and period, branch, class, insurer, client and currency, and identifies generation date and user while distinguishing draft, pending, approved and posted. The management dashboard covers premium production, earned and deferred commission, client receivables, insurer balances and remittances, claims exposure, cancellations and refunds, client-money and operating-bank positions, foreign exchange and profitability by branch, insurer and class, with actual, forecast and pending amounts distinguished. All financial reports reconcile to the general ledger and supporting subledgers.
items.note: Actual-versus-forecast presentation is present in the production report; branch-level profitability depends on branch dimensions being populated.

items.decision: Accounting dates follow the Africa/Kampala business day rather than the database's UTC date. A document's posting date, a receipt's voidable date, the closed-period test, accounting-setting lookups and statutory-parameter lookups all resolve against the Kampala day. This determines which accounting period a transaction between 00:00 and 03:00 Kampala time falls into.
items.note: Business-date functions are business_today() and ins_local_date()/ins_local_today(). The same day applies platform-wide from 20261122090000 and 20261122100000.

items.decision: An endorsement is unwound as its own approved document before a policy may be cancelled. Its credit notes are voided, its open items cleared through the endorsement clearing account, and the commission it booked is returned to unearned rather than left recognised. Nothing is deleted: the reversal is a set of journals that mirror the original line for line.
items.note: Where commission was already transferred to operating funds, the clawback becomes a recoverable and client money is replenished.

items.area: Opening position, retained earnings and migration balancing
items.decision: Earned commission up to cut-over is carried in opening balances through retained earnings (3200) and only the unearned remainder is deferred in 2020. Opening balances post through the opening balance clearing account (3900) and must balance to zero before the position is accepted. A correction after posting requires an explicit reopen with a recorded reason.
items.note: Control totals are re-applied across the gate-hole fixes of 20261110180000 and 20261111090000.

items.area: Broker-fee classification and its accounting and tax treatment
items.decision: A brokerage fee is a distinct supply from premium and from a statutory charge, recognised in 4100, and is VAT-exempt by default as an insurance service. A separate non-brokerage service is classified other_taxable_service with a stated reason and is standard-rated at the governance-held rate. Fee classification, not a company-level switch, governs the treatment.
items.note: Fees invoiced before 17 November 2026 keep their VAT because that output tax was declared.

unbuilt.requirement: Commission recognised in proportion to premium collected on agreements that are pro-rata rather than binary.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Allows commission income to be earned gradually; keeps the uncollected portion in 2020. Without it a pro-rata agreement is either recognised too early (at_placement) or too late (whole commission on final receipt).
unbuilt.acceptance: A partial collection of 50% of premium earns exactly 50% of commission, the remainder stays in 2020, a further collection earns the balance, and voiding a receipt reverses only the portion that receipt earned.
unbuilt.note: Built as a FOURTH mode, preserving the binary on_premium_collection rather than replacing it (decision 1A). Recognition is earned in proportion to premium collected; the uncollected portion stays in 2020. The build is code-complete and parse-checked but has never been executed: eval must pass before any sign-off treats it as proven, and the register's A3/A4 implemented flags stay false until then.

unbuilt.requirement: A receipt taken before bind is held as a client-money liability (2040) and released against the policy receivable when a policy binds, or refunded.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Without it a pre-bind receipt is either unallocated cash or wrongly recognised premium. The liability must never be netted against insurer payable.
unbuilt.acceptance: A receipt with no policy creates a 2040 credit and no receivable; binding a policy allocates it and clears 2040; an unallocated advance is visible on the client statement as a liability and is refundable.
unbuilt.note: Complete in two halves, which is why the status lagged. 20261124010300 added account 2040 and the advance lifecycle: a pre-bind receipt sits in 2040 with no receivable created, so AR is not overstated by money taken before placement, and it can be refunded. The release-on-bind half waited for B11's disposition primitive, because a party balance could only move by cash or a same-role credit note; it now posts Dr 2040 / Cr 1100 with the bank untouched. An approved refund above a threshold additionally needs an approved request, per B7.

unbuilt.requirement: Binding refuses unless an explicit recognition mode is approved and in force for that policy's insurer agreement. No silent fallback to on_insurer_settlement.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Prevents an unclassified insurer agreement from being accounted for on the historic default, which overstates or understates earned commission depending on the true agreement.
unbuilt.acceptance: A policy on an insurer with no configured mode cannot bind and the error names the insurer and the missing setting; configuring the mode allows the bind and the chosen mode is frozen into the accounting snapshot.
unbuilt.note: TWO HALVES, BUILT AT DIFFERENT TIMES. (1) Fail-closed bind: 20261124010200 already refuses to bind when no approved ins.commission_recognition is in force, testing the setting's SOURCE rather than its value, because acct_get_setting returns the seeded default with source='default' and a value test would never fire. (2) PER INSURER (decision 2B): 20261124011000 adds ins_insurer_commission_terms -- the mode agreed with one insurer, for a period, with the clause it rests on, proposed and approved by two different people. One company-wide setting cannot express a book written on several bases at once, which is the normal case for a brokerage. Precedence at bind is now: gross_premium settlement basis, then a per-policy override, then the insurer's approved terms in force on the inception date, then the company setting, then refusal. The refusal names the insurer (name AND code) and both places the mode could have come from, because telling someone only about the company setting sends them to the wrong screen when the answer was supposed to be an agreement. The snapshot records commission_terms_id and commission_terms_ref, so a mode can be defended later without re-deriving which terms were in force. ins_commission_mode_readiness() shows, per insurer, whether policies will bind and why -- a refusal is only useful if the gap can be seen before a client is at the counter. DESIGN NOTES: a separate table rather than a column on ins_insurers, because a mode is a term of an agreement with an effective period and an approver, and a renegotiation must leave last year's mode attached to last year's policies. Approved terms are immutable: they are ended with a date and replaced, so both remain readable. The mode vocabulary comes from accounting_setting_definitions.implemented_values, the same registry the company setting uses, so the two cannot drift. NOT DONE, stated plainly: there is no backfill, and that is deliberate. Seeding every existing insurer with its current effective mode would stamp a decision nobody made, which is precisely what fail-closed exists to prevent; the readiness report is the tool for closing the gaps, insurer by insurer, with a human on each. Until each insurer is either covered by terms or by a reviewed company default, BINDS FOR THAT INSURER WILL FAIL -- this is the intended behaviour and the main pre-merge risk. Also unbuilt: currency, branch and department are not part of the routing key for terms, and the multi-insurer (co-insurance) case takes the policy's insurer_id, not each share's insurer.

unbuilt.requirement: Cancellation request date, effective date and financial settlement date are recorded separately, with evidence required for a backdated effective date.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Decides which period a cancellation posts to and prevents a settlement date being used as the coverage date.
unbuilt.acceptance: A cancellation requested in period 1, effective in period 2 and settled in period 3 posts to the settlement period while reporting its effective date; a backdated effective date without evidence is refused.
unbuilt.note: CENSUS BEFORE BUILD: two of the three dates already existed under other names -- proposed_at is the request date and posting_date is the date the approval posts -- so only ONE column was missing and only one was added. A second source of truth for a fact the system already knows is a bug waiting to diverge. BUILD: (1) ins_policy_cancellations.settlement_date, stamped at posting from the cash rather than typed in. (2) ins_cancellation_date_evidence, holding the dated instruction or notice a backdated effective date rests on; recordable only before the cancellation posts, because a justification added afterwards is not evidence. (3) ins_cancellation_settlement_date() derives the period from fin_settlements: a cancellation produces TWO open items with different source_types and different source_ids (ins_cancellation_client_refund keyed to the cancellation, ins_cancellation_insurer_recovery keyed to an adjustment row), and each side can clear on its own date, so the period is the LATEST of the two. Matching on one source_type would silently have found only half the money. (4) The backdating rule is checked twice: at submission, so the person hears about it immediately, and again in a BEFORE trigger at posting, so removing the evidence afterwards does not help. (5) Posted dates are frozen. WHY post_journal_entry WAS NOT TOUCHED: pinning the accounting date inside it would have put a cancellation rule into the posting path of every module on the platform. The date is derived from the data that already proves it instead, and the stored value is checked against the derivation rather than trusted. FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING: the baseline immutability guard ins_cancellation_evidence_guard() diffs the whole cancellation row against a short allow-list, so a new column is refused outright -- posting would have failed with 'proposal inputs cannot be rewritten'. That function is re-issued with settlement_date added to the list and every other rule reproduced unchanged. The new evidence-table guard is deliberately named ins_cancellation_date_evidence_guard: using the existing name would have replaced, silently and successfully, the guard that three append-only tables depend on. LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: the settlement date is stamped when the cancellation posts, so a refund that clears in a later period is recorded against the earlier period unless the cash came first. The alternative is a re-dating step after posting, which the pack forbids ('closed periods are never silently rewritten'), so this is a design boundary rather than an oversight, and it should be settled at the accounting-policy gate.

unbuilt.feature: Claim stage model and the two review states (built)
unbuilt.requirement: Eight stages: reported, assessed, internally approved, insurer confirmed, funded, partially paid, fully paid, closed, plus the Coverage under review and Payment disputed states.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Internal approval must not create a payment posting; recognition must follow the insurer's confirmation, and a disputed payment must not be recognised as settled.
unbuilt.acceptance: A claim moves through all eight stages with an audit row each; internal approval creates no journal; insurer confirmation creates the receivable; partial payment leaves a visible balance; a disputed payment is excluded from settled totals.
unbuilt.note: Built additively. The eight stages are COMPUTED by ins_claim_stage() from status, recognised_at and posted payments -- nothing is stored, so a stage cannot drift from the ledger. ins_claim_payments.kind already separates insurer_receipt (funding) from client_payout, which is what makes funded/partially_paid/fully_paid derivable. The two review states ARE stored (coverage_under_review, payment_disputed) because they are judgements, not totals, and both require a note. ins_claims_guard now refuses recognition while coverage is under review, per pack 7.3. ins_create_claim accepts an out-of-period loss only with an explicit acknowledgement plus a reason, and records late_notification. The status vocabulary was NOT renamed: it is referenced by ten functions including void_journal_entry() and ins_cancelled_policy_guard(), and a rename of that breadth in an unreplayed migration is a worse risk than the gain. v2 7.2 lists eight stages and omits repudiation; the state exists and is needed, so it is kept and reported.

unbuilt.requirement: A manual-journal path requiring a balanced entry, finance maker and independent checker, evidence and reason, subledger reference for control accounts, immutability, and reversal instead of editing.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Without it any correction outside the documented flows happens as raw SQL, which has no maker-checker and no subledger reconciliation.
unbuilt.acceptance: A manual journal cannot post unbalanced, cannot be approved by its maker, cannot post to a control account without a subledger reference, and cannot be edited after posting.
unbuilt.note: CENSUS CORRECTED, 24 Nov: the earlier census said three of the four criteria were met by ABSENCE. Two are met by a real control that has nothing to do with the grant on post_journal_entry. check_journal_entry_balanced is a DEFERRED CONSTRAINT TRIGGER on journal_entry_lines (baseline), so an unbalanced entry cannot be committed by anyone, including service_role and the table owner -- deferral is what lets the per-line inserts inside post_journal_entry work at all. prevent_journal_mutation blocks UPDATE and DELETE on both journal tables for everyone, with the single documented exception of voiding. So balance and immutability were always enforced; what was genuinely missing is the feature itself. BUILD: fin_manual_journals and fin_manual_journal_lines, written only through fin_create_manual_journal / fin_submit_manual_journal / fin_decide_manual_journal / fin_withdraw_manual_journal. Approval and posting are one step, so there is no window where a journal is approved but unposted or posted but unapproved. The ledger primitive stays exactly as locked as it was: post_journal_entry is called only from the approval function, after the checks, under source_type 'manual' so the existing reports that look for it keep working. CONTROL ACCOUNTS: a line on an account with is_control_account must name a subledger source type and id, and the check resolves that to a real open item in this company whose control_role posts to that same account. A reference that does not resolve is refused, because it looks reconciled while being nothing. The check runs at creation, again at submission, and again at approval -- cheap, and the failure it prevents is a subledger that silently stops agreeing with the ledger. DELIBERATE CHOICES: lines freeze the moment the journal leaves draft, not only once it posts, so the figures approved are the figures that post. A manual journal cannot be dated in the future and cannot land in a closed period. It is a company-finance instrument, so the gate is the finance role and company administration, NOT can_access_insurance() -- a company without the insurance module must be able to write one. WHAT THE PACK ASKS FOR THAT THIS DID NOT DO AT THE TIME: section 11 wants amount-based approval limits and escalation on manual journals too. B7 built that engine for refunds only, so at B6 the gate was maker-checker plus the finance role with no threshold routing. THAT GAP IS NOW CLOSED by B12, which routes a manual journal through every configured level before it posts. What B12 still does not do is escalation, and routing by currency, branch or department.

unbuilt.requirement: Amount-based approval limits by transaction type, currency, role, level and branch, with escalation, plus detection of transaction splitting.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: A control, not a posting: it governs who may release refunds, remittances, commission transfers and claim payments.
unbuilt.acceptance: A refund above a user's limit routes to the next level; the same user cannot approve it; two same-day refunds to the same payee just under the limit are flagged as a possible split.
unbuilt.note: CENSUS 24 Nov 2026: a threshold-routing engine ALREADY EXISTED and is reused rather than duplicated. workflow_stages carries threshold_amount, approver_role, sequence_order, next_stage_low_id/next_stage_high_id, blocks_offer_submitter_approval and is_finance_terminal_stage; approval_assignments carries threshold_max; approval_actions records decisions. All 14 configured stages were applies_to='requests' with procurement roles, so no insurance refund was wired into it. BUILD: (1) extends the applies_to vocabulary with 'insurance_refunds' (workflow_stages is left otherwise untouched, and the existing 'requests' and 'invoices' behaviour is unaffected). (2) approval_actions was NOT reused: its request_id is NOT NULL and references requests(id), so it is procurement-only and cannot hold a refund. Two tables carry refunds instead -- ins_refund_requests freezes the required stage, level and role at request time, and ins_refund_approvals records each decision with its stage, level and approver. (3) platform_ins_refund_required_level() returns the highest active stage whose threshold the amount reaches, and NULL means no limit is configured, so a company that configures nothing keeps exactly today's behaviour rather than being silently blocked from refunding. (4) Level and the approver's OWN limit are separate refusals: an amount can be a level-1 refund and still exceed what that particular user may sign off, which is why approval_assignments.threshold_max is checked as well. (5) ins_refund_client_advance is re-created to refuse a refund above the threshold unless an approved request covers it. Without that last piece the whole workflow is advisory, because the money-moving function could be called directly. (6) A split is a FLAG, not a block, per pack wording: two same-day refunds to the same client whose combined value crosses a threshold are recorded on the second request with the figures that triggered the flag, and it is left to the approver to decide. LIMITS OF THE BUILD, stated plainly: currency, branch and department are not part of the routing key -- the requirement names them and this build routes on amount only, with the approver's role checked for the stage. approver_role must be one of the labels the two role tables can hold (finance or cost_control, or admin, manager, member); any other label raises INS_REFUND_ROLE_UNCONFIGURED naming the problem, and a company administrator can always decide. The build covers refunds of client advances; remittances, commission transfers and claim payments do not yet route through it.

unbuilt.requirement: Recovery types (overpayment, third-party, insurer underpayment, instalment), disputes, authorised write-offs and adjustments.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Without recoveries and write-offs, an overpayment to a claimant stays on 2030 indefinitely, overstating the client claim payable.
unbuilt.acceptance: A recovery is raised against a claim, allocated when received, and never touches commission accounts; a write-off requires approval and posts to an identifiable account.
unbuilt.note: Both halves are built. Write-offs: ins_write_off_claim charges the claim payable to a named expense account (20261124010500). Recoveries: ins_claim_recoveries, raised as a SEPARATE receivable with its own payer rather than as a negative claim -- an insurer underpayment is not owed by the client, and re-pricing the claim would disturb every report already relying on the approved amount. The test asserts raising a recovery leaves the approved amount and the accrual count unchanged. Commission accounts (4000/2020/1110) are refused by name at raise, per pack 7.7. Receiving goes through the ordinary settlement path so every cash guard applies. Writing off a recovery charges the loss back to the account it was credited to when raised (stored on the row, no default), so the net result on that account tells the truth. OPEN QUESTION Q4 in Appendix B: which account absorbs a recovery credit -- the code takes it as an argument.

unbuilt.feature: Daily client-money reconciliation and shortage response (built)
unbuilt.requirement: A daily reconciliation prepared by one officer and independently reviewed, with a client-money position test at commission-transfer time, escalation of missed reconciliations, and a shortage incident flow.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Client-money protection. Without the position test a transfer can leave the client-money account short even though each individual posting was valid.
unbuilt.acceptance: A transfer that would leave the client-money position negative is refused; two consecutive missed reconciliations escalate; a shortage raises an incident and blocks further transfers until independently released.
unbuilt.note: EXECUTED, 24 Nov 2026: test_client_money_controls.sql runs end to end on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM) -- 21 statements, all pass -- after being corrected against the functions that implement the behaviour. It had never run. Execution exposed that the fixture was describing a product that does not exist: a policy inserted directly (ins_policies_guard refuses it), commission marked earned on an unfunded policy (the funding guard refuses it), a subledger liability ALSO posted to the GL so the same obligation was counted twice (the position read 20,000 where the section states 400,000), a reconciliation recorded for the wrong day for the streak assertion, and fixtures dated on the business date, which makes an accounting-setting approval effective that day impossible (ACCT_SETTING_BACKDATED). It now does what a company does: create, submit, approve, bind, collect through the maker/checker cash path, remit to the capped amount. See docs/insurance-brokerage/EXECUTION_LOG.md.

unbuilt.feature: Beneficiaries, death claims and instalment settlements (built)
unbuilt.requirement: Authorised representatives reporting after a policyholder's death, multiple beneficiaries with percentage or fixed allocations totalling 100%, disputed shares held until determination, and instalment settlements each with their own dates, amounts and evidence.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Determines who is paid and when; a disputed share must never be redistributed automatically and an instalment receipt must settle the existing balance rather than create new recognition.
unbuilt.acceptance: A death claim records the representative and beneficiaries; percentages must total 100%; a disputed share is held while undisputed shares pay; a second instalment reduces the balance without a new claim accrual.
unbuilt.note: Built on the existing claim payable item; no new accounting primitive was needed. Percentage OR fixed allotments, either alone or mixed, must total the approved claim amount -- a death benefit that allocates only part of itself would leave an amount nobody is entitled to. The held-share rule is enforced by a DEFERRED constraint trigger, because the claim has ONE open item and the payment rows are inserted after the settlement: only a deferred check sees the whole transaction. A held share contributes nothing to what is payable and is never redistributed. Editing allotments is refused if it would put payable below what has already been paid, which is how a dispute would otherwise be nullified after the money went out. Instalments carry expected date, actual date, amount and evidence, and settle the existing approved balance -- the test asserts the accrual journal count is unchanged after a second instalment. Death claims require the representative and the authority relied on (probate, letters of administration, mandate).

unbuilt.requirement: An advance held on 2040 can be released against a bound policy of the same client: 2040 falls, AR falls, cash does not move, and both open items show the consumption.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: Without this an advance can be taken and refunded but never applied, so premium paid before placement stays on 2040 until it is either refunded or posted again. 2040 is correct; the mechanism to clear it against a policy is missing.
unbuilt.accounting_basis: The subledger records party-balance movement in exactly two ways: settlement allocations (cash) and same-role credit notes. A cross-role reclass is a third kind, and does not exist.
unbuilt.acceptance: A release of 250,000 leaves 2040 down by 250,000 and AR down by 250,000 with the bank unchanged; the open item shows the consumption; over-release is refused; a write-off reduces 2030 into the named expense account; commission accounts are refused; a control account cannot be the counterparty; a disposition cannot be edited or deleted.
unbuilt.note: Built as one primitive serving both needs. fin_open_item_dispositions records a non-cash movement of a party balance, and fin_open_item_consumed() now counts posted dispositions as a third source, so every existing guard and the ageing view see the reduced balance without being touched. The consumption arithmetic moved into fin_open_item_consumption_v so the function and fin_open_item_balances cannot disagree. Advance release is Dr 2040 / Cr AR, forced by double entry. A write-off needs an account the policy chooses, so the caller MUST name it: it must be a non-control account and it may not be a commission account. Choosing that account here would be the software inventing accounting policy. OPEN QUESTION for the accountant (Appendix B): which account absorbs a claim write-off.

unbuilt.feature: Multi-level approval for manual journals (built, executed)
unbuilt.requirement: A journal routed above approval level 1 must be approved at every level it routes through, by the role each level names, before it posts -- and splitting approval across levels must not be satisfiable by one person.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: A control, not a posting. It decides who must agree before a correction reaches the ledger, and it is the difference between a company being able to configure an amount limit and being able to use it.
unbuilt.acceptance: A journal routed to level 3 posts nothing until three distinct entitled people have approved, in order; one signature at level 1 does not post it; the raiser cannot sign any level; the same person cannot sign two levels; a level whose role nobody holds is reported as unconfigured and a company administrator can unblock it; a missing stage in the sequence is refused rather than signed by anyone; a rejection at any level rejects the journal and posts nothing.
unbuilt.note: EXECUTED, 24 Nov 2026: test_fin_manual_journal_chain.sql runs end to end on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM) -- 25 statements, all pass. It had never run. TWO PRODUCT DEFECTS came out of it. (1) The sequence-gap check refused EVERY approval when any later level was unconfigured, so a correctly authorised level-1 signature on a journal whose level 2 was missing was refused with FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_CHAIN_GAP -- the journal was stuck rather than its misconfiguration reported. It now fires at the level being signed and never on a rejection, since a refusal posts nothing and blocking one only traps the journal. (2) create or replace with extra DEFAULTED parameters created an OVERLOAD rather than replacing ins_create_claim, leaving two functions that both accept a six-argument call, so every six-argument call raised 42725 regardless of argument types. Also corrected: two fixtures asserted things the product contradicts -- a staff_roles row on module 'finance', which platform_modules makes non-entitlable, and a journal raiser who was not on the finance team, which fin_create_manual_journal refuses.

unbuilt.feature: Transfer lock: zero-tolerance preconditions (built, single-connection executed; two-connection lock race unexecuted)
unbuilt.requirement: The commission-transfer guard must not permit the same earned commission to be moved twice, and its lock ordering must be a property of the function rather than an accident of where blocks happen to sit.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: A control, not a posting. It decides whether commission can leave client money more than once for the same entitlement.
unbuilt.acceptance: An entry already sitting on a posted transfer is refused when named by a new transfer; the entry selection and its locks happen in one statement; and a clean transfer, including the no-entries pool path, is unaffected.
unbuilt.note: CORRECTS AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS REGISTER. It was recorded that the guard had a reachable double-post race because the aggregate that chooses entries and the separate lock that covers them ran as two statements. That was too strong and is now withdrawn: 20261124011200 also takes a policy-level lock BEFORE the aggregate, over the same policies, so two sessions cannot reach the aggregate concurrently for the same entries. The race I described was not reachable. What IS true, and is what this migration fixes, is that the safety was distributed across three places in the file and could be removed by a later edit without any test noticing -- exactly how the position test became unreachable once before, which the file itself records. TWO CHANGES: (1) an entry already sitting on a POSTED transfer is refused (INS_TRANSFER_ALREADY_TRANSFERRED). This matters because ins_void_commission_transfer sets entries back to status 'earned' with transfer_id NULL, so 'earned' does not mean 'never transferred'; the check is on the requested entries only and is skipped when p_entry_ids is null, because an entry on a posted transfer cannot be selected by the pool in the first place. (2) the aggregate and its locks are folded into one CTE with ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE, and the locked set is re-verified against the requested set, so under READ COMMITTED a concurrent commit yields fewer rows and is refused rather than silently changing v_total. NOT FIXED, stated: the guard is still per-company serialisation rather than per-policy (throughput, not correctness); and there is no database-level uniqueness preventing one entry appearing on two transfers, because voiding resets entries rather than marking them. EVIDENCE: supabase/tests/test_client_money_controls.sql §6 covers the permitted path, the re-transfer refusal, the reset-but-still-posted case and the pool path, and has been EXECUTED on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM) with all 21 statements passing; the two-connection lock race in scripts/test-ins-commission-transfer-concurrency.ts remains unexecuted because PGlite is single-connection.

unbuilt.feature: Currency in the approval routing key (built, partly exercised)
unbuilt.requirement: Approval limits must be evaluable by transaction type, amount, currency, role and approval level, so a company working in more than one currency can express a separate limit in each.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: A control, not a posting. Without it a multi-currency company has one limit that is only meaningful in one currency.
unbuilt.acceptance: A USD-configured tier does not route a UGX journal; an untrimmed or lowercase currency code still matches; and a caller that supplies no currency matches only any-currency stages, so a tier can never be applied to the wrong money.
unbuilt.note: CLOSES AE5 CONDITION C4. workflow_stages.currency added, NULL meaning any currency and defaulting to NULL so every existing row and every amount-only company is unchanged. platform_approval_required_level(uuid,numeric,text,text) compares threshold per currency; the three-argument form is DROPPED rather than replaced, because CREATE OR REPLACE cannot change a parameter list and an overload would have left the old currency-blind function alive and chosen. platform_manual_journal_chain_state reads fin_manual_journals.currency, so a USD tier cannot route a shilling entry. ins_request_refund passes v_adv.currency, so a currency-specific refund stage fires instead of being dead. TWO OVERLOADING TRAPS FOUND AND FIXED BY RUNNING THEM, both invisible to a parse check or a CREATE: a three-argument refund helper with a default collides with the existing two-argument one and two-argument calls fail with 42725 'function is not unique'; the same is true of a four-argument form that keeps a default on its third parameter. The shipped two-argument signature is therefore kept as-is and the currency-aware form has three REQUIRED parameters, which cannot be confused with two. Verified against a live database: all three arities resolve, a UGX tier reaches level 2 for UGX and stays at level 1 for USD and for a no-currency call. NOT DONE: branch and department are still not in the key -- a branch is not unambiguously readable from a journal, and inventing a column to satisfy a checklist would put a control on a guess; there is no uniqueness on (tenant, applies_to, sequence_order, currency), so two stages can silently occupy one level for one currency; and the second refund call site (in ins_decide_refund) still passes no currency, so a currency-specific refund stage is applied at request time and not re-checked at decision time.

unbuilt.feature: Correct and resubmit a rejected manual journal, scoped by approval round (built, executed)
unbuilt.requirement: A rejection must stop the chain and return the journal for correction or cancellation, and the audit trail must preserve every submission, approval, rejection and resubmission.
unbuilt.accounting_impact: A control. It decides whether a corrected entry keeps one traceable history or becomes an unrelated replacement journal.
unbuilt.acceptance: A rejected journal can be reopened by its raiser with a reason and resubmitted; the corrected round counts zero prior approvals; the rejected round's approvals and rejection remain on record; the same people may sign the corrected round; and the raiser still cannot approve it.
unbuilt.note: EXECUTED, 24 Nov 2026: test_fin_manual_journal_resubmit.sql runs end to end on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM) -- 17 statements, all pass. It had never run. THE RESUBMIT PATH WAS UNREACHABLE ON A FRESH DATABASE and this is why: 20261124011900 re-issued the two-argument refund lookup with a widened OUT list, which PostgreSQL accepts on an empty database and refuses with 42P13 'cannot change return type of existing function' on any already-provisioned one -- a migration that only applies to a virgin schema is not a migration. Both defects in this file's dependency chain (that one, and the plpgsql-body validation that made 20261124010300 unappliable) were found by running the stack, not by reading it.

decisions.summary: Dedicated contra-claims-expense account, tenant-assigned code. Posting is Dr 2030 / Cr that account.
decisions.insurer_receivable: Pursued separately; not written off with the claimant payable.

decisions.summary: Release only; no automatic forfeiture income. Forfeiture needs a separately authorised decision with evidence.
decisions.refund_approvals: Independent second approver on every client-advance refund, regardless of amount.

decisions.summary: Repudiation is the ninth claim state; record the insurer's decision, date, reason and correspondence; allow reopening.
Recoveries credit the contra-claims-expense account; not netted into insurer receivables by default.
Free client money continues to deduct insurer receivables. No code change; the shipped enforce default matches.

acceptance_evidence._comment: How much each claim in this pack has actually been demonstrated, as distinct from built. Agreed with the reviewer on 24 November 2026. A guard-level probe and an end-to-end workflow are NOT interchangeable evidence, and neither satisfies UAT acceptance: UAT is a business user executing the complete workflow in the application, which nothing in this repository can evidence from a SQL session.

levels.deliberate_behaviour_change: Behaviour differs from what is currently shipped, on purpose. Requires an approved behaviour specification, regression tests for both the permitted and the prohibited action, and a named authorised correction route. Not a defect and not silently absorbed.
levels.guard_level_verification: The guards execute, their ordering behaves as specified, and the tested conditions produce the expected decision. Does NOT establish document creation, persistence, financial posting, related-record updates, rollback behaviour, permissions across the workflow, or completion through the user interface.
levels.end_to_end_not_demonstrated: Integration tests using realistic records with complete persistence and posting assertions. Currently absent for the affected workflows.
levels.uat_pending: A business user executes the complete workflow successfully in the application. Pending for everything in this pack.

items.subject: The policy-level lock in ins_transfer_earned_commission

behaviour_specification.what_changed: Concurrent commission transfers now serialise on the set of insurance policies that have earned commission, before any client-money position is read. Previously nothing serialised them.
behaviour_specification.which_actions_become_unavailable: None that were available in a non-competitive run.
behaviour_specification.trigger_condition: Two or more sessions transferring earned commission for the same company at the same time.
behaviour_specification.observable_effect: The second session waits until the first commits or rolls back, then is judged against the position the first one left behind. It may then be refused, and the refusal is the pre-existing INS_TRANSFER_POSITION / INS_TRANSFER_TRUST_SHORT — not a new error code. A single caller sees no difference.
behaviour_specification.harm_prevented: Two transfers each reading a sufficient free position and both passing, together overdrawing client money.
behaviour_specification.authorised_correction_route: Unchanged and not narrowed. An over-transfer is corrected the same way it was before: a bank payment moving the money back, and the position is then what it is. Nobody needs a new permission to fix it. The lock ends when the transaction ends — it is not a sticky block, it cannot be released, and it cannot be forgotten. The sticky block in this area is the shortage incident, which is a separate control with its own independent release (ins_release_shortage).

items.required_evidence: Approved behaviour specification; regression tests for the permitted and the prohibited action; a two-connection test proving the second transfer is refused.
evidence_present: supabase/tests/test_client_money_controls.sql  (single-connection permitted and prohibited paths: §1 clean transfer succeeds, §2 position test refuses) -- EXECUTED, 24 Nov 2026, PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM), 21 statements, all pass
docs/insurance-brokerage/EXECUTION_LOG.md  (harness, shims, and the fixture defects that execution exposed)
evidence_missing: A two-connection concurrency test. The existing harness (scripts/test-ins-cancellation-cash-concurrency.ts) requires a local disposable *_cash_test database and two psql connections. It could not be run in the environment where this change was verified: no psql client and no Docker. THE LOCK IS THEREFORE UNPROVEN. It is correct by reading and by PostgreSQL's documented semantics for SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and that is all.

items.subject: Guard-level probes of the client-money position, approval limits and claims-account readiness
evidence_present: Executed on a live PostgreSQL database inside a rolled-back transaction, 24 November 2026:
the client-money position function compiles and returns (the column-ambiguity defect that threw on every call is fixed);
an unconfigured company acquires no manual-journal approval level, while a refund from the same company still falls back to its mandatory second finance approver;
a 60,000,000 journal routes to level 2 and is refused at submission with FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_LEVEL and stays in draft; a 40,000,000 one submits;
ins_posting_role_readiness() reports an unmapped claims account, flips to mapped when one is assigned, and names the same account ins_claim_contra_account resolves;

Re-run of the migration stack and five test files, 24 Nov 2026, on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM): 143/143 migrations apply to an empty database, and test_fin_manual_journal_chain, test_fin_manual_journal_currency, test_fin_manual_journal_resubmit, test_fin_manual_journals and test_client_money_controls all pass. Six defects that made migrations unappliable or controls unreachable were found by this and are listed in EXECUTION_LOG.md; four assertions that contradicted the product were corrected against the implementing function.

items.subject: Full document workflow for the commission transfer, manual journal, refund and claim write-off paths
items.required_evidence: Integration tests using realistic records, with complete persistence and posting assertions.
items.note: Some of this is closer than the classification suggests, and it is worth knowing which. supabase/tests/test_client_money_controls.sql is written as a genuine integration test: real gl_accounts, real fin_bank_accounts, real ins_commission_entries, real fin_open_items and a real post_journal_entry, asserting the resulting position and the posted transfer. It was NOT counted as end-to-end evidence because it had never been executed. Attempting to execute its fixture on 24 November found that it could not have been: it inserted a `currency` column into ins_commission_entries, which has never had one (information_schema returns zero rows for it, in the baseline and in every later migration), and it created a bound policy with status 'active' while leaving bound_at null and net_premium_to_insurer unset, which violates ins_policies_bound_check. Either would have stopped the file at its own helper function, before a single control was exercised. Both are now fixed. The file is STILL UNRUN: executing it needs the full B9 migration applied alongside it, and that combined payload exceeded the SQL transport used for verification. Its design is end-to-end; its status remains unproven.

items.subject: Business-user execution of the complete workflow (UAT)

items.subject: Manual journals routed above approval level 1: a refusal replaced by an approval chain (B12)
items.approved_by: reviewer, 22 November 2026 -- approved in principle, conditional on eight named controls. As of 24 November 2026 all eight are met: C1 routed journal enters workflow; C2 levels in sequence; C3 maker-checker separation; C4 thresholds and roles applied against amount, CURRENCY and transaction type (B14); C5 a rejection stops the chain and returns the journal for correction (B15); C6 posted journals immutable, corrected by reversal; C7 missing configuration fails closed; C8 audit preserves every submission, approval, rejection and resubmission (B15). The evidence for the manual-journal chain, the currency key, the resubmit path and the single/multi-level paths has been EXECUTED, not merely written: see docs/insurance-brokerage/EXECUTION_LOG.md. The row remains a production-go-live blocker only for AE3 (no document workflow demonstrated) and AE4 (no UAT), which are separate rows and are not satisfied by executing guards.

behaviour_specification.what_changed: A manual journal routed to a level above 1 used to be REFUSED AT SUBMISSION with FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_LEVEL. It is now accepted for submission and held: it posts only when every level from 1 to the routed level has been approved, in order, by distinct people holding the role each level names, none of them the person who raised it.
behaviour_specification.which_actions_become_unavailable: The action that becomes genuinely unavailable is the one that was never correct: posting a routed journal on a single signature. Concretely, a user holding only the finance role can no longer complete a routed journal alone; the person who raised a journal can no longer approve it at any level, including as a company administrator; one person can no longer take two levels of the same journal; and approving a level whose role you do not hold is refused. The one refusal that was removed -- submitting a routed journal -- was a wall, not a control, because it blocked the entry entirely rather than routing it.
behaviour_specification.trigger_condition: The company has active workflow_stages rows with applies_to = 'manual_journals' whose threshold_amount the journal's total_debit reaches, and the highest such stage has sequence_order > 1. With no stages configured nothing changes: required_level is 0 and the pre-existing single-checker rule applies unchanged, which is a fallback control and not a bypass. Also triggered by a gap in the configured sequence, which is refused.
behaviour_specification.observable_effect: Submitting a routed journal returns pending_approval instead of raising. Deciding below the routed level returns pending_approval and posts nothing; the last level posts. New error codes each naming the problem: FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_ROLE, FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_ROLE_UNCONFIGURED, FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_DISTINCT, FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_CHAIN_GAP, FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_STATE. FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_LEVEL no longer exists as a refusal.
behaviour_specification.harm_prevented: An entry the company said needs higher authority passing on one signature -- either by being approved at level 1, or by a shell chain in which one determined person signs every level. Also prevents a hole in the configured sequence turning into a level anybody at all may sign.
behaviour_specification.authorised_correction_route: A level whose role nobody holds: a company administrator may sign any level, and the error says so. A stranded or misconfigured chain: change the stage approver_role through the platform-admin-only RPC update_workflow_stage_approver_role, which refuses a blank role. A journal that should not proceed: any user entitled to decide the current level may reject it with a reason, and it closes as rejected with nothing posted. NOTE: correcting a rejected journal currently means raising a new one -- there is no edit-and-resubmit path, which is condition C5 below and is not met.

conditions.requirement: A routed journal must enter the configured approval workflow rather than being rejected merely because it requires multiple levels.
conditions.note: Built; proved by test_fin_manual_journal_chain.sql §2. Executed on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM), 24 Nov 2026.

conditions.requirement: Each approval level must be completed in sequence.
conditions.note: The next level is derived as the lowest 1..required_level with no approval, so out-of-order signing is impossible rather than merely refused. §2. Executed on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM), 24 Nov 2026.

conditions.requirement: Maker-checker separation must remain enforced; the maker cannot approve their own journal.
conditions.note: Checked before any level is considered, so it applies at every level including to company administrators. §5 and §1b. Executed on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM), 24 Nov 2026.

conditions.requirement: Approval thresholds and roles must be evaluated against the journal's amount, currency and transaction type.
conditions.note: Amount, currency, role and transaction type are all evaluated. Currency was the gap: workflow_stages gained a currency column (NULL = any, so amount-only routing is unchanged for a company that never sets it), platform_approval_required_level takes the currency of the money and fails closed when it is not supplied, the manual-journal chain reads the journal's own currency, and ins_request_refund now passes the advance's currency so a currency-specific refund stage actually fires (B14). Proved live: a USD tier cannot capture a UGX journal, an untrimmed 'usd ' matches 'USD', and a null currency matches only any-currency stages. Still absent: branch and department, which remain unbuilt because a branch is not unambiguously readable from a journal.

conditions.requirement: A rejection must stop the chain and return the journal for correction or cancellation.
conditions.note: Both halves now hold. Stopping the chain was already true: a rejection at any level closes the journal, records the level that refused it, and posts nothing. Returning it FOR CORRECTION is now built (B15): fin_reopen_manual_journal takes a rejected journal back to draft, limited to the raiser or a company administrator, and only with a reason. Only 'rejected' can be reopened -- a posted journal is still corrected by reversal, a withdrawn one stays withdrawn.

conditions.requirement: A posted journal must be immutable; subsequent corrections require an authorised reversal or adjustment.
conditions.note: Pre-existing and not weakened by B12: prevent_journal_mutation blocks UPDATE and DELETE on both ledger tables for everyone, voids are the single documented exception, and manual-journal lines freeze at submission rather than at posting.

conditions.requirement: Missing or invalid approval configuration must fail closed, not bypass approval.
conditions.note: Four fail-closed paths: a gap in the sequence is refused (FIN_MANUAL_JOURNAL_CHAIN_GAP); a level with no approver_role is refused rather than read as 'anyone'; a role no user holds is refused as UNCONFIGURED with company administration as the documented route; and no configuration at all falls back to the pre-existing finance-or-admin single-checker rule, which is a control already in place, not the absence of one. §§8-9. Executed on PostgreSQL 19.0 (PGlite/WASM), 24 Nov 2026.

conditions.requirement: Audit history must preserve every submission, approval, rejection and resubmission.
conditions.note: Submission, per-level approval, rejection, reopening and posting are all recorded, and now on the SAME journal rather than split across a replacement. fin_manual_journal_approvals carries an append-only row per decision with its round, level, stage, the role required on the day and the comment; nothing is deleted when a journal is reopened, so the rejected round remains readable beside the corrected one. log_platform_event records submission, each level approval, the rejection, the reopen and the post. RESIDUAL: a journal submitted by a company with no chain configured writes no chain event, which is correct but worth knowing when reading the trail.

items.required_evidence: Tests for single-level and multi-level approval; tests proving the correct approval order; tests proving maker-checker separation; tests proving missing configuration blocks posting safely; and an end-to-end routed-journal test demonstrating submission through final posting.
